content.summary: Casey Tran (TUTOR) reports that in bilingual review export EX-51, a Vietnamese diacritic appears as a question mark in the downloaded CSV, while it displays correctly in the browser preview. Morgan Hale (TEAM_LEAD) replied asking Casey to save the original export and note the application used to open it, stating that it has not been established where the character change occurs. No cause or fix has been identified.
content.central_question: In the bilingual review export EX-51, why does a Vietnamese diacritic appear as a question mark in the downloaded CSV although it looks correct in the browser preview, and what should be done about it?

attributed_agent1_resolution.rationale: The only reply is a request for evidence (the original export file and the application used to open it) and explicitly says the point of change has not been established. This is diagnostic evidence gathering, not a conclusion or guidance about the diacritic corruption, even though the author is a TEAM_LEAD.
attributed_agent1_resolution.note: Agent 1 label, not evidence; NEEDS_REVIEW means Agent 1 did not verify it. Assess resolution from the member messages.

content.summary: Jamie Park (TUTOR) reports that the CSV for EX-67 shows a missing accent in one editor while the web preview still shows it; no other editors have been checked. Morgan Hale (TEAM_LEAD) replies with troubleshooting steps: download the file from Export History, keep the original file, try a UTF-8 editor, and report whether the downloaded text still differs. No cause or conclusion about the missing accent is established.

attributed_agent1_resolution.rationale: The only reply gives diagnostic steps and asks for a follow-up report on whether the downloaded text still differs. That is evidence gathering, not a conclusion about the cause or the correct handling, so the issue remains open even though the author is a TEAM_LEAD.

detail_sentences.text: A tutor reports that the Vietnamese diacritic on EX-51 is replaced with a question mark in the downloaded CSV but looks correct in the browser preview.
A different tutor reports that the CSV for EX-67 shows a missing accent in one editor while the web preview still has it, and has not checked any other editor.
In the EX-51 thread the team lead asked the tutor to save the original export and the application name, and said it has not been established where the change happens.
In the EX-67 thread the team lead asked the tutor to download from Export History, keep the original file, try a UTF-8 editor and report whether the downloaded text still differs.

The current troubleshooting FAQ says to preserve the downloaded file, compare the original bytes or a UTF-8-aware rendering with the web preview, record the export ID and viewer, and keep the cause open until the original is checked.
